protocol: bench-spec.md §2; peak RSS sampled at 100 ms by harness/run-bench.ps1; first run on a cold file cache discarded and reported separately

runs.note: cold run: module load + Defender scan; every later run of the same shape is ~0.2-0.3 s
single run: a second run would cost another 9.4 minutes, so the 3-run median was not affordable here; documented deviation from bench-spec.md §2

scaling.verdict: superlinear: 5x the sources costs ~31x the time. Reproduces the upstream report that getWebTreeMapData dominates at 10k files (source-map-explorer#186).

conclusion.small_real_projects: no pain: 0.22-1.65 s and 31-49 MB, dominated by process start-up
conclusion.large_maps: real, reproducible pain: 18.4 s at 7 MB, 9.4 minutes at 36.5 MB, 277-642 MB RSS
conclusion.implication: the Nopeat stop-the-line condition R1 (>1 s on realistic maps) is NOT triggered for small projects, but IS triggered for large ones; the product case is therefore about the large-project segment, and the positioning must say so explicitly
conclusion.open: the source-map-explorer baseline phase breakdown is still unmeasured (SME does not report per-phase timings); the win mechanism (zero-allocation VLQ + binary search over sorted mappings) is therefore still a hypothesis until B5 is run
